title: Journal Club: Building a Better Chloroplast

reader_summary.headline: Hello, I'm Lauren Richardson, and this is the A16Z BioJournal Club.
reader_summary.overview: Hello, I'm Lauren Richardson, and this is the A16Z BioJournal Club. This is our podcast where we cover recent scientific advances, why they matter, and how to take them from proof of principle to practice. In today's episode, I'm talking with Bio Deal Team partner, Judy Savitzkaya, a resident expert in all things synthetic biology.

key_points.text: We cover recent research that seeks to improve the processes of photosynthesis and carbon fixation and how these advances could one day be used to improve crop growth and carbon sequestration in plants..
key_points.evidence_quote: We cover recent research that seeks to improve the processes of photosynthesis and carbon fixation and how these advances could one day be used to improve crop growth and carbon sequestration in plants.

key_points.text: During photosynthesis, also known as the light cycle.
key_points.evidence_quote: During photosynthesis, also known as the light cycle, light energy is captured by chlorophyll and then pass through a series of reactions to the energy-rich chemical co-factors, ATP and NADPH.

key_points.text: These co-factors are then used by the carbon fixation cycle or dark cycle to drive the capture and conversion of carbon dioxide into more complex carbon molecules like glucose..
key_points.evidence_quote: These co-factors are then used by the carbon fixation cycle or dark cycle to drive the capture and conversion of carbon dioxide into more complex carbon molecules like glucose.

key_points.text: Plants and other phototrophes use these two processes to turn sunlight and carbon dioxide from the air into organic matter.
key_points.evidence_quote: Plants and other phototrophes use these two processes to turn sunlight and carbon dioxide from the air into organic matter.
